title: Casper and the Summer
premise: Edmund Galloway inherited Hollowmere Vineyard along with its crushing debts, and he has spent three years keeping it alive through a lucrative but soulless contract with a corporate distributor. When a freak June snowstorm strands him at the estate with Marguerite 'Margot' Chen — the rival vintner who broke his heart in their twenties — and her business partner Julian Ashe, the man who now holds both their futures in a bidding war, old wounds and older feelings resurface over barrels of his late grandfather's forgotten reserve wine. As the summer solstice festival approaches, Edmund discovers the reserve could clear every debt without selling to Julian, but only if he and Margot can collaborate long enough to prove its worth. At the festival's final tasting, Edmund must choose between signing Julian's career-saving contract and pouring the reserve with Margot; he chooses her, they win the crowd, and the debts are cleared on their own terms.
about_author: Orsen Vane is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent a decade working harvests across the Rhône Valley before turning to fiction. They write romances about second chances, stubborn land, and the people who refuse to leave either behind.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Rows
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Three years after inheriting Hollowmere's debts, Edmund walks the vineyard at dawn, tallying what the distributor's contract demands versus what the land can give. A letter from Julian Ashe's firm announces an inspection visit. The beat is weary resignation laced with quiet love for a failing place.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Julian arrives charming and surgical, offering a contract that would save Hollowmere but strip Edmund of every decision, including the cellar. Edmund signs nothing yet. The beat is the seduction of relief and the first flicker of resistance.

chapters.title: A Forecast No One Believed
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The regional forecast calls for an impossible June snowstorm. Edmund prepares the estate alone until a car slides into the ditch at his gate: Margot Chen, rival vintner, stranded. The beat is shock curdling into dread as he recognizes her.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Trapped by the storm, Margot catalogs everything she never said after their twenties ended badly — a stolen harvest idea, a betrayal she committed and he never learned the full shape of. The beat is guilt wearing competence as armor.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Seeking shelter from a burst pipe flood, they discover his grandfather's hidden reserve: unlabeled bottles of extraordinary wine, forgotten for decades. Margot tastes one and goes still. The beat is wonder breaking through hostility.

chapters.title: Julian's Weather Advantage
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Stranded too when his return flight cancels, Julian realizes the reserve is an asset worth owning and begins quietly positioning himself between them. The beat is ambition disguised as helpfulness.

chapters.title: Snow in the Vine Rows
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Forced to work together protecting the vines from unseasonal frost, Edmund and Margot fall into old rhythms — hands brushing, arguments that feel like flirting. The beat is warmth against cold, muscle memory of intimacy.

chapters.title: The Harvest We Stole
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Margot finally confesses the truth of their twenties: she took credit for his blending method to save her family's winery, then fled before he could hate her properly. The beat is confession met not with fury but with grief.

chapters.title: Blind Tasting
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. To test the reserve honestly, they run a blind tasting; Edmund realizes Margot's palate is the only one sharp enough to help him bottle it before the solstice festival. The beat is reluctant trust taking root.

chapters.title: Contract on the Table
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian offers Margot a partnership that would make her rich and separate her from Edmund permanently, framing it as rescue. She hesitates. The beat is temptation with a countdown clock.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In his grandfather's ledger, Edmund finds notes suggesting the reserve was meant to be shared — a blend intended for two families, theirs and the Chens'. The beat is inheritance redefined as instruction rather than burden.

chapters.title: Barrels and Blame
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A blending session collapses into recrimination: whose fault was the lost decade, whose pride, whose silence. Margot storms into the storm itself. The beat is the midpoint rupture.

chapters.title: Night in the Frost House
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund finds Margot sheltering in the old frost house; neither can sleep, and they talk until dawn about timing, debt, and who gets to begin again. The beat is raw honesty without resolution.

chapters.title: Julian Moves First
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Roads reopen early for one convoy; Julian secures a distributor meeting on festival day and tells Edmund the reserve deal dies unless he signs by sundown tomorrow. The beat is the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Method, Remembered
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Margot publicly credits Edmund's blending method in front of visiting buyers, undoing her decade-old theft in the only currency the industry respects. The beat is restitution offered at real cost to herself.

chapters.title: Two Signatures
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Edmund drafts a joint bottling agreement naming both vineyards; Margot signs. Julian learns of it and warns them the festival tasting will be rigged against unknowns. The beat is alliance sealed under threat.

chapters.title: Bottling Day
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The whole estate — staff, neighbors, Margot's crew — bottles the reserve in one feverish day. Edmund admits to himself he isn't choosing between wine and Margot anymore; he's choosing a life. The beat is joy earned through labor.

chapters.title: Eve of the Solstice
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. On the festival eve, Julian makes his final offer to Margot alone: sign with him tonight and Hollowmere's contract vanishes, saving Edmund's land but ending them. The beat is the cruelest kindness, refused.

chapters.title: The Festival Pour
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the solstice festival, the rigged tasting order buries them last; Edmund chooses the moment — pours the reserve instead of signing Julian's contract, telling the crowd whose wine it truly is. The beat is the climax: public choice, no retreat.

chapters.title: What the Crowd Decided
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The room turns; orders come in; Julian, outmaneuvered by honesty rather than strategy, concedes with unexpected grace and withdraws the contract. The beat is defeat transformed into respect.

chapters.title: First Light on Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Debts settled by the reserve's sales, Edmund rewrites the ledger's last page and asks Margot to stay — not as partner or penance, but as herself. The beat is tenderness after courage.

chapters.title: Caspar and the Summer
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Epilogue at next year's bud break: the vines thrive, a new label bears both names, and Margot reflects that second chances were never about timing — only about who stays to see them through. The beat is quiet, certain happiness.
